context: The prompt is framed entirely around the deploy stampede, and the stampede has a reflexive answer, so the predicted baseline failure is that the agent replaces RETRY_DELAY_MS with a doubling schedule, adds jitter, writes docs/reconnect-policy.md about backoff, and stops - treating the accept-log sample as the scanner the on-call called it. That sample is the part with teeth. src/reconnect.js reconnects on every close event and never looks at the code it was given: `socket.on('close', () => retry())` discards the argument entirely, so a client whose session the gateway has revoked with 1008 comes straight back, one second later, forever. Backoff does not touch that loop - it only slows it - because the connection succeeds every time before the server closes it, and `socket.on('open', () => { attempts = 0; })` resets the counter on every one of those successes, so maxAttempts never engages no matter how it is configured. That is why one session in the sample has been cycling since 2026-08-27 and why 617 sessions account for 184,000 of 187,000 accepts in a window with no deploy in it. A conforming client treats a close code as the server telling it whether to come back; 1008 says the connection was refused on policy grounds and retrying cannot change that. The third predicted failure is a suite that cannot detect the absence of what was added: a test that ticks the clock and asserts a reconnection happened passes identically against the fixed interval, the doubling schedule and the randomised one, and a jitter assertion over an uninjected Math.random() is a coin flip that will eventually fail in CI.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: test/reconnect.backoff.test.js and docs/reconnect-policy.md both exist and src/reconnect.js has been changed. Any one of the three missing scores at most half; producing only the source change scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT reconnect after a close the server used to refuse the client
checklist.description: The delivered src/reconnect.js MUST NOT schedule another attempt after a close code of 1008, and the delivered suite MUST NOT be green against an implementation that ignores the close code. Full marks require all three: the close handler reads the code it is passed, a policy close ends the reconnect loop permanently rather than delaying it, and a test drives a socket that opens and is then closed with 1008 and asserts that no further connection is opened however far the clock is advanced. Leaving `socket.on('close', () => retry())` discarding its argument scores zero for this criterion regardless of what else was fixed. Slowing the retry after a 1008 instead of stopping scores zero - the loop in the accept sample is a slower loop, not a fixed one. Stopping on 1008 in source with no test that would catch its removal scores at most half. Treating other non-retryable endings the same way - 1002, 1003, or a clean 1000 - is correct and does not reduce the score; treating 1006 or 1011 as non-retryable does, since those are the endings the reconnector exists for.

checklist.name: The attempt cap actually engages
checklist.description: A connection that opens and is immediately closed by the server counts as a failed attempt. As shipped, `socket.on('open', () => { attempts = 0; })` clears the counter on every cycle, so maxAttempts can never be reached by a client that keeps being accepted and then closed - which is every session in the accept sample. The delivered suite must include a case that opens and is closed with a retryable code each time and assert the client gives up after maxAttempts. No such case scores zero. Changing the source so the counter survives a short-lived connection but covering it with no test scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT ship a retry schedule every client agrees on
checklist.description: A hard-coded reconnect interval with no jitter is the anti-pattern under test. The delivered src/reconnect.js MUST NOT produce the same delay for the same attempt number on every client. Leaving RETRY_DELAY_MS as the delay scores zero. A purely deterministic backoff - 1s, 2s, 4s with no randomisation - scores at most half, because a fleet disconnected together still returns together, in fewer and larger pulses. Full marks require randomisation in the delay plus a test that fails if the randomisation is removed.

checklist.name: Growth, ceiling and a decidable jitter assertion
checklist.description: The suite asserts that successive delays grow rather than repeat and that growth is bounded by a ceiling, and the jitter assertion is decided rather than sampled - either because the random source is a constructor option with a default that the test drives with fixed values, or because the delay is bounded so the assertion holds for any draw. Calling Math.random() inside the module and asserting two runs differ scores at most half; it is a test that fails on its own schedule. No assertion on any delay value scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT measure the schedule with real time
checklist.description: The new tests MUST NOT use real timers, await a sleep, or set a test timeout to wait out a delay; the injected clock in testutil/clock.js exists for this. Any real-time wait in the delivered suite scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Policy document says both what the client waits and when it stops
checklist.description: docs/reconnect-policy.md gives the concrete schedule - base delay, growth, ceiling, randomisation range - and states which endings are retried and which end the loop, by code. A document that describes backoff and never says that some endings are not retried at all scores zero, however complete its schedule is; one that names the non-retryable endings but gives no numbers for the schedule scores at most half.

checklist.name: Published signature and existing suite intact
checklist.description: createReconnector still accepts the same options and still returns start / stop / attempts / delays, test/reconnect.basic.test.js is byte-identical to the fixture, and npm test passes. Editing the basic test to accommodate the new behaviour scores zero.
